_comment: Terms taught without corpus evidence. docs/vocabulary-system.md §2 places these in T6 (private banking / structured products), whose target material is not in content/corpus — so the gate cannot pass them on frequency alone. Every entry must state WHY the term earns its place and WHEN that claim gets re-checked. An entry with no reason is not a justification, it is a silencer; the validator rejects those.
_rules: reason must name what the term is for, not restate the term
reviewBy is a date, not a promise: on/after it the validator fails the build until the entry is re-justified or removed
replacing an entry with corpus evidence is always better than renewing it

pledge.reason: The pack's headline pair with hedge. The distinction (protect vs collateralise) is the whole thesis of the course; no headline in the corpus uses the word because journalists say 'securities-backed loan' instead.

collateral.reason: The asset side of every secured loan; required to explain haircut and margin call. Corpus headlines name the lender's action, not the asset.

haircut.reason: The one number that decides how much can be borrowed against a pledge. Sourced to FINRA/SEC SBLOC investor alert (sources: finra-sec-sbloc-2015).

margin call.reason: The failure mode the whole course warns about; paired with haircut and leverage. Sourced to the same FINRA/SEC alert.

leverage.reason: Names the position size that a margin buffer supports — without it, margin has no purpose in the sentence.

derivative.reason: The category that option/put/call/futures/swap all belong to; the pack teaches the family, so the parent term is needed.

option.reason: One of the two instrument families the pack contrasts (with futures/swap).

put.reason: The concrete instrument behind the hedge example ('buy a put so a crash hurts less'); the example sentence is meaningless without it.

call.reason: The put/call pair is the pack's instrument axis; teaching one without the other breaks the sibling relation.

short selling.reason: The opposite-direction strategy the course contrasts with hedging; needed for the 'same bet, different name' unit.

notional.reason: The denominator of every leverage and derivative statement; without it the sizes in the examples are unreadable.

basis risk.reason: The reason a hedge can fail even when the direction is right — the course's honest-caveat term.

diversification.reason: The non-instrument way to reduce risk, declared as a confusable relation with hedge.

counterparty.reason: Who is on the other side of the derivative; paired with default in the risk unit.

default.reason: The event that makes collateral and counterparty matter; the pack's risk story terminates here.

mark-to-market.reason: How a pledged position gets re-priced, which is what triggers a margin call. Sourced to the FINRA/SEC alert.

securities-backed loan.reason: The actual name of the product the pack is about; it is the term the corpus uses INSTEAD of pledge, so it anchors the synonymy the learner must recognise.

capital gains.reason: The tax reason the buy-borrow-die pattern exists. Sourced to IRS Topic 409 and Publication 551.

buy-borrow-die.reason: The named strategy that ties the pack's lending and tax threads together; sourced to the University of Chicago Press monograph.

real rate.reason: Nominal minus inflation; the one true confusable pair with interest rate in the legacy pack (same word root, different quantity).

quantitative easing.reason: The central-bank tool whose mechanics explain why real rates can go negative; the pack's macro thread.

spot.reason: The other end of the futures axis; the pack teaches the curve, so both endpoints are required.

contango.reason: One of the two curve shapes; teaching one without the other leaves the shape unnamed.

backwardation.reason: The opposite curve shape; declared as the sibling of contango.

cost of carry.reason: The mechanism that decides which curve shape you get; the causal term behind contango/backwardation.
